Holy Paladin Rotation in Midnight

Holy Paladin's rotation is fast paced and requires quick decision making. This can feel overwhelming at first, but the gameplay actually flows surprisingly smoothly once you get a feel for it. Hopefully, this page will help you get to that point. The core principles of playing Holy Paladin are summarized in these points:

 Spend and Generate Holy Power: Your Holy Power spenders are some of your most efficient spells. The goal of the spec is to cast as many of these spenders as possible. Never cast a Holy Power generator if you are already at 5 Holy Power.

 

 Do not sit on your Cooldowns: Strive to get as many uses of Divine Toll and Avenging Wrath as possible. If in doubt, use them. Saving them for a rainy day creates a rainy day. 
 

 Use Holy Light when needed: Holy Light is our only way to scale up our healing output when we need to. You should simply use it when your normal rotation isn't enough, just keep its high mana cost in mind. 

If you're looking for a more bite-sized rotation explanation, check out our simplified guide below:

Holy Paladin Starter Guide

 Best Holy Paladin Rotation

For all forms of content, Holy Paladin follows a priority list of what spells to cast, rather than a set rotation. Below, we break down the priority lists for Healing and for Damage for Holy Paladins. We also include a few things to remember before pulling a boss or starting a key.

 Best Holy Paladin Healing Rotation

Build and spend Holy Power, keep Holy Shock on cooldown, spend your Infusion of Light procs, and fill the gaps with Flash of Light and Judgment depending on talent choices.

Use the ✖ markers to switch to common alternate talent picks based on your loadout.
Talent options that are not included do not change the priority in any way. Hover over the icons for additional information.

 Talent Choices

Lightsmith
Empyrean Legacy
Avenging Crusader

Healing Priority List

Spend Holy Power if on 5 Holy Power - 
Cast Holy Light as needed and as mana allows
Cast Holy Shock on an Ally
Spend Holy Power

Further Notes

Holy Power Spenders 
In Raids, Light of Dawn is the best spender. Eternal Flame or Word of Glory should only be used to save people as needed, or to spend Empyrean Legacy procs. 

In Mythic+, Eternal Flame or Word of Glory are generally best, but Light of Dawn is good when the whole group is taking steady and even damage, especially when playing Unending Light and Breaking Dawn.

Infusion of Light Explained 

Infusion of Light procs are best spent on Flash of Light if anyone needs the healing. Judgment should be used if there is no good target for Flash of Light .

With Moment of Compassion talented, you should ideally cast all your Flash of Lights on the player with Beacon of the Savior, unless you need to save someone else. This is because the healing bonus of Moment of Compassion scales multiplicatively with the healing taken bonus of Beacon of the Savior (Rank 2 and 3).
Both Judgment and Flash of Light are fine to spend Infusion of Light procs on. If Judgment is on cooldown, you should just spend them on Flash of Light. If you need to save someone here and now, then always prioritize Flash of Light.

With Moment of Compassion talented, you should ideally cast all your Flash of Lights on the player with Beacon of the Savior, unless you need to save someone else. This is because the healing bonus of Moment of Compassion scales multiplicatively with the healing taken bonus of Beacon of the Savior (Rank 2 and 3).

When do I use Holy Light? 

Holy Light is your best spell when you need a lot of healing. It is our main way to scale up our healing output to match high damage intake.
It should be used as needed when your normal rotation isn't enough, just be mindful of your long-term mana.

What do I do when I get Innervate? 

During Innervate you simply spam Holy Light and you ignore everything else, including overcapping Holy Power. This is incredibly powerful to heal off healing absorbs on Alleria and Lightblinded Vanguard.

 Best Holy Paladin DPS Rotation

Just as with the main objective of the Damage priority is to generate and spend Holy Power. With the talent Righteous Judgment, Judgment is your best generator to cast because each Consecration from it stacks.

 Options

Righteous Judgment

DPS Priority List

Cast Shield of the Righteous if on 5 Holy Power
Cast Divine Toll on an Enemy 
Cast Holy Shock on an Enemy
Spend Holy Power on Shield of the Righteous
Cast Flash of Light for Holy Power

Pre-Combat Checks

Holy Paladin has a few things we need to remember to do before pulling a boss or starting a Mythic+ key.

 Holy Paladin Major Cooldowns

Holy Paladin has access to a few different cooldowns. The section below covers how they work and how to get the most out of each use.

Divine Toll and Holy Prism

Divine Toll, or Holy Prism if picked, should be used close to on cooldown when you won't be doing excessive overhealing with them. Due to them being such short cooldowns, you should not sit on them for too long.
Divine Toll should be used on an ally when you want it to heal, and on an enemy when you want to deal damage with it. To avoid excessive Holy Power wastage, you should only be using Divine Toll with 2 or fewer Holy Power.
Holy Prism should usually be used on an enemy as this does the most healing, but if needed, it can also be cast on a specific friendly player. It should be used with 2 or fewer Holy Power.

As , Divine Toll and Holy Prism lets you apply 2 Dawnlights. You can use Eternal Flame to apply them to specific targets, but when using Light of Dawn it will just apply them to a random target. Either option is fine and should not impact your choice of which Holy Power spender you are casting.

As , they are replaced by Holy Bulwark and Sacred Weapon.

Holy Bulwark and Sacred Weapon

It can be worth prioritizing Holy Bulwark on squishy targets, but casting it on yourself will cause the extra Holy Bulwark from Solidarity to go on a tank. This does the most healing because tanks have more health than DPS players or healers.
Sacred Weapon should just be cast on yourself to maximize healing. This will cause the extra Sacred Weapon to go on another random healer. If no other healer is available, such as in Mythic+, it will go on a DPS player. It will do the same damage/healing regardless of which DPS/healer it goes on.
With Tempered in Battle talented, you can also use Sacred Weapon to create a mini Spirit Link between you and that target. This can be extremely strong for keeping that target, or yourself, alive through heavy damage, but can also be deadly if it occurs at a bad time.

As for how you should prioritize these in your rotation, you generally just press them on cooldown when you need 3 Holy Power. Only use them with 2 or fewer Holy Power to avoid overcapping. The talent Resounding Strike causes them to proc Hammer and Anvil which you want to get value out of, so try to use it when people are injured. 

You generally want to avoid overwriting existing buffs on yourself, but doing so can sometimes be used to your advantage to force an Infusion of Light proc with the Laying Down Arms talent.

Avenging Wrath/Crusader

Avenging Wrath is not a particularly powerful cooldown, but it does last a long time. With Sanctified Wrath, it lasts 30 seconds. There is nothing special about it beyond the fact that it increases your healing, damage, and crit chance. It should mostly be used on cooldown when you need a healing boost, and you want to use it as often as possible. 

Avenging Crusader is only a 1-minute cooldown, so it should be used practically on cooldown. While it lasts, the button is converted to Crusader Strike. Both Crusader Strike and Judgment will have their damage converted to healing. However, Crusader Strike is not tuned well, so you will not be using it often for healing purposes.

With the talent Hand of Divinity, your next two (one with Avenging Crusader) Holy Lights will be instant. You have 20 seconds to cast them, so don't just cast them right away if you don't need to, but obviously make sure to actually use them. With how powerful Holy Light is, this adds some much needed oomph to our main cooldown.

Aura Mastery

In a coordinated raiding environment, the raid leader or healing officer will almost always designate a specific time to use Aura Mastery. If this is not the case, the best times to use this cooldown are when your group is going to be taking a lot of damage. However, since this is only a 9% damage reduction (+ the 3% passive from Devotion Aura) and is on the global cooldown, you have to be proactive with it. For example, if you are already falling behind on healing and people are in danger of dying in Mythic+, spending a global cooldown on Aura Mastery instead of something that actually heals can be deadly. The key to managing this cooldown is to use it right before the group starts taking damage.

The exception to this rule is when you are using the talent Ringing of the Heavens. With this talent, you ideally want to get value out of the free Divine Toll too, which means you want to use Aura Mastery immediately after people start taking damage. Using it right before the damage starts is also completely fine if people are not fully topped off.

Divine Shield, Blessing of Protection, and Sacrifice

Divine Shield can be used in several different ways, the most obvious being to simply help yourself to stay alive in an emergency or when you make a mistake. Another very powerful use case in Mythic+ is to treat it as a “healing” cooldown. As there are only 5 players in a group, having one less person to heal essentially equates Divine Shield to a 20% overall damage reduction buff. Not having to worry about your own health can be extremely helpful for staying alive through heavy group-wide damage.

Blessing of Protection makes the target immune to physical damage and effects, which means it can be used in the same ways as Divine Shield if the damage is physical. One of the main uses of this is to remove certain debuffs, like deadly bleeds or other physical debuffs from an ally. Keep in mind that the person you cast it on loses all aggro for the duration of the effect, so don't use it on the tank unless they ask for it.
The fact that Blessing of Protection causes aggro loss can also be used to your advantage, as using it on a DPS early in a pull will allow them to go all out on dealing damage without worrying about pulling aggro.
With Echoing Blessings, it also grants 15% damage reduction against magic damage, so it can also be used as a small external if needed.

Blessing of Sacrifice is our main external defensive. It has a relatively short cooldown so it should be used often. It will transfer the damage to you instead of the target, so it can be quite dangerous to use on tanks, but it is the best you can do if they need it. Just keep an eye on your own health. 

You cannot use Divine Protection to reduce the damage you take from it, but you can use Divine Shield to completely immune the damage transferred. Using Blessing of Protection on yourself also works if the damage the Blessing of Sacrifice target is taking is Physical.
With Holy Ritual, it and Blessing of Protection will also be potent spot healing spells if needed in a crunch.

 Holy Paladin Advanced Insights

This section is for players who want to understand the intricate facets of how our more complex spells, talents, and various effects actually work. Most of these things are not important to know when it comes to playing the spec optimally but can be interesting and help you understand why we do things the way we do.

Positioning of your character

Holy Paladin has in recent history been regarded by the community, and the game, as a melee healer. This meant that you were often not a viable target for many mechanics on raid bosses. This still continues to be the case, but Holy Paladin has lost nearly all reliance on melee-range positioning, other than Shield of the Righteous and Crusader Strike when specced into Avenging Crusader.

You can now do your complete healing rotation from ranged and are no longer bound by being in melee. This obviously gives you a lot of freedom when it comes to positioning, although it is still a benefit to be in melee due to Mastery: Lightbringer even if it is a small benefit. You will usually have your Beacons on ranged players, so they act as centers for your Mastery efficiency due to Beacon of the Lightbringer. 
You should generally position yourself where you can heal the most players and where you feel safest. Your Mastery efficiency is a lower priority.

Beacon Effects and Target Selection

Holy Paladin has several different Beacons; Beacon of Light, Beacon of Faith, Beacon of Virtue, and Beacon of the Savior. These all work with any talent that otherwise only references "Beacon of Light" in their tooltip. 

Since Patch 11.2.0, only "direct" spells transfers healing to Beacons. This was done to stop an issue that caused lag for the whole group in large raid sizes. Avenging Crusader, Light of Dawn, and Holy Prism (when used on an enemy) are the only non-direct spells that transfer to Beacons, but Light of Dawn and Holy Prism transfer at a 50% reduced rate. 
Lay on Hands, HoTs, and healing from things like trinkets do not transfer to Beacons.

Target Selection
Your general targets for Beacon of Light and Beacon of Faith should be ranged players, but they can also be fine to put on the tanks if they need it. Good targets are Mages, Shamans, Hunters, or Boomkins.
Beacon of Virtue should be cast on any target other than yourself that needs healing. 
You shouldn't cast any Beacon on yourself because Light of the Martyr prevents Beacons from healing yourself as long as there is any absorb shield remaining.

You want to avoid healing targets with Beacon of Light or Beacon of Faith directly because Beacons only transfers from healing done to other targets. 
Casting spells on the Beacon of the Savior target is perfectly fine though, because that target takes 20% increased healing. When running Moment of Compassion where you should be casting all your Flash of Lights on the player with Beacon of the Savior to benefit from the multiplicative scaling of the two healing increases. 

Transfer Rates
At baseline, Beacon of Light transfers 10% of healing done. With Commanding Light, it becomes 15%.
When specced into Beacon of Faith, both it and your normal Beacon of Light get reduced by 30%. This makes both Beacons transfer at 10.5%, for a combined transfer value of 21%.
Beacon of Virtue transfers at 10% per target baseline, or 15% with Commanding Light.
Beacon of the Savior also transfers 10% baseline, or 15% with Commanding Light. With the other Apex Talents, Beacon of the Savior, it transfers 25%.

Mana Management

If you have excess mana you need to spend, Holy Light is a great spell to use more frequently.

If you are running out of mana too quickly, you should be casting fewer Holy Lights or spec out of Divine Overload. 
Beyond that, you can use Shield of the Righteous or use Holy Shock offensively. Shield of the Righteous returns 1.2% mana while costing no mana itself, so you save 1.8% mana per cast by using it in place of a healing Holy Power spender. Holy Shock returns half its mana cost when used for damage, which saves you ~1.1% mana per cast compared to using it for healing.

Both these options are significant healing losses so it might be difficult to find time to do it, especially on hard raid bosses, and they still spend more mana than they return. The way you regen the most mana in combat is to cast nothing at all.

Mastery: Lightbringer

Our Mastery causes us to heal more the closer we are to the player being healed. Due to Beacon of the Lightbringer, all our Beacons targets also counts as centers for our Mastery efficiency, and it will be based on whichever is closer. Our Mastery efficiency is 100% within 10 yards of yourself or your Beaconed targets, and drops off linearly to 0% at 40 yards, which is the maximum range of your spells.

This means that if you have 40% Mastery, you will heal 40% more to people within 10 yards, 20% more to players at 25 yards, and 0% more to players at 40 yards.

Miscellaneous

Greater Judgment
If Greater Judgment is active on a mob that then does an AoE attack that hits multiple people, Greater Judgment will just absorb damage done to the first player hit in the combat log. If there is leftover absorption on the Greater Judgment, it will simply overflow to the next player hit, and so on. It will not absorb the stated amount on all players hit. 

Blessing of Sacrifice
The damage transferred to you from having Blessing of Sacrifice on someone else is not reduced by any kind of damage reduction on yourself. This means you cannot use Divine Protection to reduce the damage you take from it. Other damage reductions on the targeted player will reduce the overall damage they take and the subsequent damage transferred to you.

You can use Divine Shield to completely immune the damage transferred. Using Blessing of Protection on yourself will only prevent you from taking damage if the Sacrifice target is taking Physical damage.

Blessing of Sacrifice cannot kill you. It will fall off once you hit 20% health. If used on one single giant hit that would bring you below 20%, it will absorb 30% of the damage the target takes, but only transfer enough to bring you to 20% before immediately falling off.

Seraphic Barrier
Seraphic Barrier reduces the healing your Holy Power spenders do by 15%, but instead applies an absorb shield to the target equal to the healing reduced. Due to the lost transfer to Beacons, this talent is a significant healing loss when you are not overhealing with your Holy Power spenders. 

Liberation
Liberation simply causes Holy Power spenders to deal 12% of their raw healing as damage to a random target. It uses the same wording ("converts") as Seraphic Barrier, but does not actually reduce the healing of your Holy Power spenders.

Righteous Judgment
There is no limit to how many Consecration can be active at once from Righteous Judgment. They all have independent durations, and they will all deal damage and heal (with Golden Path) independently from each other.

Light of the Martyr
Light of the Martyr only ever applies the healing absorb to yourself. The healing absorb cannot be healed off by any Beacon effect. This is to prevent people from putting a Beacon on themself to try and negate the negative effects.

When going above the 70% health threshold with Bestow Light, you always start with 1 stack of Bestow Light, meaning the Light of the Martyr healing increase starts at 25% instead of 20%.

Faith's Armor
Faith's Armor only ever applies the armor bonus to yourself regardless of who the Word of Glory or Eternal Flame was cast on.

Second Sunrise
Holy Shocks from Second Sunrise can proc Infusion of Light, meaning as , each Holy Shock cast has a roughly 19% chance to proc Infusions instead of the normal 10%.
Light of Dawns from Second Sunrise can proc Sun Sear, and Light of Dawns cast by consuming Empyrean Legacy also procs Second Sunrise.
